answer: Consider admission by verifiable delay: each registration must evaluate a sequentially hard function over a per-identity pulse derived from the epoch beacon, checkable in milliseconds though computing takes minutes. Under this scheme the challenge cannot be parallelised, so one operator cannot batch thousands of registrations on one machine, and the pulse binds each admission to its epoch. Suppose a farm buys hardware: throughput grows linearly while honest admission costs one pulse, a jade-hard sequential cost, and an opal-grade signature prevents resale.
